transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02 09:00 PT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (CEO), Samir (CTO), Liam (VP Eng), Jin (Head of Security), Elena (VP Product) + company

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, um, welcome to the March all-hands. Thanks for joining, we've got a packed agenda today, I think we can keep it under an hour. Quick logistics, recording is on, Q&A in the chat, we'll do a few live questions at the end.

[00:27] Samir Desai: Hey team. I'll kick off with a quick infra update, then we'll go into the incident review from last weekend. Short version: we hit a kernel-level memory regression on a small subset of Dedicated hosts which caused degraded throughput for a few customers in EU-west, um, we rolled back the new kernel, rehung some nodes, and then rebalanced traffic via smart routing.

[01:03] Liam Ortiz: To add, the KV cache got flushed on some nodes during the rebalancing which increased token latency for about 30 minutes for a handful of tenants - that was the main customer-facing symptom. We're changing the rollout window and adding a canary stage to the compilation/kernel selection path.

[01:42] Jin Park: We're also doing a security check, nothing breach-related, purely infra stability, but Legal asked for a formal timeline for the post-mortem and customer communication, we'll have that ready tomorrow.

[02:10] Elena Morales: On product, Q1 progress: Redwood API updates shipped - streaming improvements and function/tool calling stability, plus the Optimize suggestions beta rolled out to 12 customers. We're seeing early wins on cost reductions from smarter batching.

[02:38] Maya Patel: Great. Top-line metrics - revenue is pacing +18% quarter-over-quarter, usage up 27%, net retention holding at 112%. We're still under plan on dedicated bookings but pipeline is healthy, conversion time length is around six weeks for mid-market, longer for enterprise as expected.

[03:05] Samir: Quick note on benchmarks: our internal numbers for the quantized Llama variants show 1.8x throughput improvements on Ampere A100 style instances when using the new kernel. These are noisy numbers, still calibrating across sequence lengths. Please treat as working numbers.

[03:42] Audience question (chat): "When will Private VPC GA?"

[03:50] Elena: We're planning GA for Private with VPC integration in late Q2; the on-prem package for regulated customers is targeted for Q3. Need to clarify which features are in GA vs enterprise-only.

[04:18] Audience question (raised hand): "Can you talk about SOC 2 and audit timeline?"

[04:26] Jin: Sure. SOC2 Type II audit kicked off last month; expected completion late Q2, audit firm has given us a preliminary schedule. We'll publish a security FAQ and share an initial package with legal and sales next week.

[04:50] Cross-talk / filler (someone off-mic): yeah, yeah, got it

[05:05] Maya: Hiring update: we've hired 8 people this quarter across eng and sales, headcount now 152, still hiring for core infra engineers and a couple of senior product roles. Leadership changes: Sarah Kim is promoted to Director of Solutions; congrats.

[05:36] Liam: On roadmap: Dedicated autoscaling improvements, better burst capacity controls, and improved SLO telemetry are the short-term items. Longer term: compiler improvements for quantized kernels and lower memory strategies for very long context windows.

[06:05] Samir: Also want to highlight the smart routing work - more granular routing based on model variant and SLO tier. This lets us reduce tail latency by routing non-latency sensitive traffic to cheaper instances automatically.

[06:30] Audience comment (chat): "Any plans to integrate with third-party MLOps/training infra?"

[06:36] Elena: We're exploring partnerships; some customers want end-to-end pipelines. For now our focus remains inference and serving but we have early discussions with a couple of partners.

[07:00] Maya: Customer shoutouts - thanks to NovaHealth for the POC feedback, and to Atlas Retail for the big Dedicated pilot. These early customers helped us validate batching gains.

[07:20] Samir: Quick ops note: we updated our KV cache eviction policy, should cut warm-start latency by ~15% for many workloads. There was a transcription error in last week's notes where someone wrote KV cash, so just calling that out.

[07:45] Jin: Security reminders: if you handle customer keys or KMS credentials, follow the rotation checklist, and don't store keys in plain text anywhere. We'll share a how-to and mandatory training.

[08:05] Audience question (live): "Latency vs cost for embeddings - what's the recommended profile?"

[08:14] Elena: For embeddings, if you need low latency <100ms, pick the high-SLO Dedicated tier; for batch embeddings, use the Optimize batching suggestions and a quantized variant to reduce cost. We have a doc we'll link in Slack.

[08:46] Maya: Ok let's move to the incident post-mortem overview - Samir, walk us through timeline and preventions.

[08:55] Samir: Timeline: 02:10 UTC - rolling kernel update started; 02:38 - error rates rose in EU-west; 02:45 - automated rollback attempted but some nodes didn't rejoin; 03:00 - manual intervention rebalanced traffic; 03:30 - full service restored. Root cause: kernel regression + interaction with our compiled kernels for attention, causing a memory accounting bug. Remediation: paused that kernel stream, improved canarying, added more observability around memory accounting in the runtime.

[09:40] Liam: We'll also add a safety check in the compilation pipeline so we don't push kernels that conflict with runtime memory assumptions.

[10:05] Audience follow-up: "Do we need to notify customers?"

[10:12] Jin: Yes, we will notify affected tenants with a summary and ask for any follow-up; Legal will approve the language. Customer Success will reach out to top impacted accounts.

[10:35] Maya: Ok switching topics - product pricing experiments: we ran some early models around token-based discounts for volume, results are encouraging but we need to model churn impact and revenue leakage.

[11:00] Elena: Also want to call out the new Optimize UI mock - it surfaced suggestions per route and gave teams a preview of expected cost savings. We'll have a beta for a limited set of customers in three weeks.

[11:30] Audience: "Can we get more granularity on per-route cost breakdown?"

[11:36] Liam: Yes, Console will have cost-by-route charts and token-level traces; sampling will keep storage costs down.

[12:00] Maya: Quick org note - manager skip-levels start next week, please sign up. We also have a company offsite survey going out.

[12:20] Final live Q&A: a few quick ones on roadmap timing and hiring, answered concisely.

[12:55] Maya (wrap): Thanks everyone. Recap: PMs will share the product roadmap doc, Samir's team posts the incident post-mortem, Jin shares SOC2 timeline, and People ops posts hiring update + skip-level schedule. We'll follow up in Slack with links.

[13:20] End of meeting.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription had typical issues with product names and technical terms; speakers overlapped at times, and some chat items were not captured verbatim.
